subject: Heartbeat mismatch across routing shards — request for SLA eligibility and postmortem
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@paylyst.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: eng+paylyst@paylyst.com
Date: Sat, 9 Sep 2028 01:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: 503 spike at 00:12 UTC — can you confirm downtime window?

Hi Priyom,

We saw a spike of 503/504 responses for our checkout route at ~00:12–00:18 UTC last night. Our payment flow dropped ~18% for about 6 minutes and we flagged it as a potential SLA incident on our side. Can you confirm what Redwood saw for Paylyst during that window and whether this is eligible under the uptime SLA?

Attached are our sampled client traces and timestamps. We need a confirmation of the exact impacted window and a log bundle to file with procurement. Also curious whether this aligns with any shard routing changes you rolled out.

Thanks — we’re under a close renewal conversation and this is time-sensitive.

—Sanjay
Sanjay Rao
Director of Engineering, Paylyst
ops@paylyst.com

Attachments: paylyst_traces_sample.csv (3KB)

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@paylyst.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 9 Sep 2028 02:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: 503 spike at 00:12 UTC — can you confirm downtime window?

Hi Sanjay — thanks for the heads up and for the trace samples. I’m escalating this internally and we’ll get an evidence bundle over to you. Initial notes:

- We observed increased 503 returns for model-routing shard group rs-13 between 00:11:50–00:18:05 UTC.
- Root cause looks like a heartbeat mismatch between two router processes that caused a short window of failed handoffs; the runtime then degraded requests to the next-available pool which added queue time and some 503s.
- We need to pull the raw router and scheduler logs (I’m requesting a bundle).

Can you confirm the earliest and latest client-observed timestamps so we can align windows? For SLA evaluation, we’ll need to verify: 1) that the error rate exceeded the SLA threshold, and 2) the outage was not an excluded maintenance window.

Monica — can you pull router logs + the KV-cache metrics for rs-13 from 00:05–00:25 UTC and attach a log bundle? Diego — please call out any active rollouts during that timeframe. I’m copying Marcus for credit/contract signoff if we determine eligibility.

I’ll send an interim status by 10:00 PT with an evidence bundle.

Thanks,
Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Priyom.Das@redwood.com

Attachments: none

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>, Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@paylyst.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 9 Sep 2028 06:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Logs and preliminary SLO calc for Paylyst 00:11 UTC window

Priyom / Sanjay — attaching the log bundle and my quick SLO worksheet. Summary:

- Collected router logs and scheduler traces for rs-13 from 00:05–00:25 UTC (redwood_logs_20280909_00-15.tar.gz).
- Confirmed heartbeat misses on router-7 between 00:11:49.7–00:14:12.2 UTC. During that window, the cluster returned 503s to approximately 3.8% of requests for Paylyst’s route, exceeding the 0.1% threshold in section 3.2 of the SLA.
- After 00:14:12 UTC the routers recovered and normal routing resumed.

I’ve put a provisional SLO impact calc in slo-calculation-sheet.xlsx and a short draft postmortem (draft_postmortem.md). The calc shows ~5.9 minutes of impacted traffic at an effective availability delta that could trigger a proportional credit under the agreement.

Forwarding the core excerpt from the router log below for visibility:

----- Forwarded message -----
From: Redwood Router <router@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 9 Sep 2028 00:12:01 UTC
Subject: heartbeat miss on router-7

[00:11:49.705] router-7 heartbeat lost to scheduler (rs-13)
[00:12:05.122] router-7 failed to handshake with pool-4, returning 503 to upstream
[00:13:48.221] router-7 rejoined cluster

----- end forwarded -----

Next steps: Marcus, can you confirm whether the contract team is able to approve a pro-rata credit if confirmed? Sanjay, we’ll queue a short postmortem and share the final evidence bundle and SLO calc by tomorrow EOD if that timeline works.

—Monica
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood_logs_20280909_00-15.tar.gz, slo-calculation-sheet.xlsx, draft_postmortem.md

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@paylyst.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 10 Sep 2028 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Heartbeat mismatch across routing shards — request for SLA eligibility and postmortem

Sanjay — thanks for the quick follow-up and for your patience. To summarize and next steps: 

1) Impact window confirmed: 00:11:49.7–00:14:12.2 UTC (6m22.5s).
2) Eligibility: Monica’s preliminary calc indicates the event exceeds the 0.1% error threshold in SLA section 3.2 for Paylyst’s production route and therefore meets the basis for a pro-rata credit. Final credit amount requires the standard pro-rata calculation (we’ve populated the inputs in the attached sheet).
3) Root cause: heartbeat mismatch on router-7 leading to failed handoffs; full RCA will include why the router missed heartbeats (config drift vs. transient GC vs. rollout timing).

Marcus — can you confirm approval to proceed with a standard SLA credit (as described in our contract) once Monica finalizes the exact credit calc? If Marcus confirms, we’ll issue a formal remedy statement and credit token to Paylyst and circulate the finalized postmortem by EOD tomorrow.

Sanjay — will that timeline work on your end? If you need an expedited credit token for procurement immediately, let me know and we’ll prioritize the billing flow.

Thanks,
Priyom
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Priyom.Das@redwood.com

Attachments: slo-calculation-sheet.xlsx (provisional)
